sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The business purchases end-of-life tyre feedstock and processes it by continuous pyrolysis into tyre pyrolysis oil, recovered carbon black, steel and syngas. Syngas supplies process energy and sodium-silicate production. Revenue depends on feedstock-to-product spread, utilization, rCB upgrading/qualification, saleable yield and working capital, not simply tonnes of waste received. FY26 parent mix was approximately 53.56% fuel oil,18.60% rCB,18.00% sodium-silicate glass and 8.44% renewable-technology solutions; these are parent disclosures, not a complete consolidated segment reconciliation. [S1 pp40–43]

Bhilwara and Dhule each operate 100 TPD pyrolysis plants. Shantol’s Dhar 100 TPD facility received consent to operate 18 May 2026 and announced commercial commencement 19 May, taking group capacity to 300 TPD. Samsara, acquired 1 October 2024, supplies crumb rubber/tyre chips and serves external customers as backward integration; it reported ₹24.0051 crore turnover and a ₹3.6448 crore loss in FY26. Its operations restarted May 2026 after the October 2025 fire. Group sales eliminate internal feedstock trades, so adding all subsidiary sales to parent sales without elimination would overstate growth. [S1 pp131–132][S20]

The parent also added machinery/gasification activities associated with Radhe. Revenue is recognized under the disclosed AS sale-of-goods/service policy, rather than an assumed multi-year executable order book. Customer-level credit terms and concentration are incomplete. An all-output sodium-silicate offtaker is now named for Dhar, but no published contract price, minimum purchase guarantee, payment security or cancellation protection supports treating the announcement as unconditional backlog. [S22]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Proposed mechanism: continuous process capability and integrated syngas use → evidenced by actual Dhule operation and reuse at Bhilwara → potentially lower energy cost and stable product → failure if virgin-carbon/oil prices fall, feedstock costs rise, recovery yields disappoint or emissions approvals interrupt operation. Certifications and commissioning are useful qualification evidence, not proof of price-setting power. rCB customer qualification is slow; management describes roughly 9–18 months depending on application. Four-wheeler tyre adoption remains gradual. [S1 pp40–43][S16]

A capable entrant needs process know-how, pollution approvals, feedstock access, stable rCB specifications and capital. Management’s approximately ₹50 crore per 100 TPD pyrolysis-plus-rCB plant is an attributed estimate, not an independently benchmarked replacement cost or assured project IRR. The controlling group and related machinery supplier may provide engineering capabilities; dependency and related-party pricing must be assessed alongside that benefit. No exclusive listed-company-owned patent rights or independently sustainable cost advantage is assumed. [S16][S1 pp126–127]

Relevant comparators are deliberately economic rather than identical: Gravita offers diversified recycling/feedstock execution and a growing rubber platform; PCBL(TN) explores TPO and sustainable carbon feedstocks within a larger conventional carbon-black business; Birla Carbon’s Continua gives customers a circular material with established formulation/distribution access. Birla is not an interchangeable listed pure-play and PCBL(TN) is not the same equity perimeter as Hi-Green. These sources establish competitive mechanisms, not a dated peer valuation table. No reliable same-cutoff three-to-five-name comparable multiple set was established, so peer multiples are ND and are not silently borrowed for valuation. [S24][S25][S26]

The correct moat conclusion is useful but contestable process competence, MOAT 5. A defined, independently verified market-share denominator is unavailable. The company’s claims about global scale remain attributed and do not earn a leadership bonus.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The growth case has three distinct stages: operating Bhilwara/Dhule capacity; commissioned Dhar pyrolysis still proving customer/rCB economics; and proposed Dhar 60 TPD silicate with a January 2027 target and approvals in process. A fourth pyrolysis plant and one-per-year expansion are not committed funded capacity. The 31 August disclosure says Dhar ran smoothly since May, but it does not publish plant cash returns. [S1][S20][S22]

The model’s base case uses 44,000→65,000 annual tyre-input tonnes, within 72,000 tonnes at the disclosed 240-day capacity convention, and 12,000→28,800 silicate tonnes across existing/proposed lines. Realization rises 2% annually; equipment and external feedstock sales are modeled separately, with internal sales excluded. Base annual capex ₹16/9/10/12/13/14 crore is an explicit pause on further pyrolysis plants after the current platform, not management’s ₹40–50 crore annual expansion ambition. It includes a conditional silicate/completion allowance and replacement investment. A sensitivity adds ₹27 crore annual capex to approximate the management program; this requires much more rescue capital. [S16][model]

The bull case separately funds a fourth 100 TPD line through ₹35 crore capex in each of FY28/FY29 and caps throughput below 96,000 tonnes. Even this is not an approved plant or proven cost estimate. The bear links weak product realization with lower margin, more working capital and cash stress, rather than independently varying price alone.

CAP remains NS. Including CWIP, goodwill, operating tax/subsidy balances, deposits and capital advances produces FY25/26 invested capital ₹134.826/155.599 crore; normalized FY26 ROIC is 6.35%. The one-year incremental book proxy is−1.92%, but its numerator mixes old-plant margin, acquisition/fire effects and capital not yet commissioned. Neither this negative proxy nor management’s future target proves new-plant destruction or attractive returns. Attributable matured cohort returns are needed. GQS remains NS because CAP and CASH are not scoreable; sales growth alone cannot substitute for quality of reinvestment.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoters held 71.9184% at 30 June 2026 and disclosed no pledge; public ownership was 28.0816%. Parent directors’FY26 remuneration of ₹0.25 crore is modest compared with ₹8.35 crore parent PAT, though additional subsidiary management pay is separately disclosed. The annual report carries an unmodified financial opinion and favorable control opinion; the auditor reports no observed fraud and no current loan default. These findings are retained, not treated as a certificate that all governance risk is absent. [S17][S1 pp55–59,126]

Related-party procurement is economically material: Radhe supplied ₹27.1939 crore fixed assets in FY26 after ₹27.1139 crore in FY25; sales plus erection/installation to it were ₹7 crore in FY26. The group has ₹10.3444 crore related loans repayable on demand. Technology/business transfer and supplier pricing, rather than mere related-party existence, are the open minority-protection questions. No allegation of diversion is made. [S1 pp114,126–127]

The 2023 offer report retains unquantified MSME interest qualifications in FY21–23. FY26 MSME principal is ₹9.8991 crore, with interest shown nil; the settlement/quantification bridge for legacy issues was not retrieved. Statutory dues were not always timely, although the auditor described delays as not serious and no undisputed dues older than six months. Secretarial observations were late forms, a clerical year error and an independent-director proficiency extension to August 2027, not automatic misconduct. Prior-tax short provisions were ₹0.5542 crore and ₹1.5995 crore in FY25/FY26. [S15 F2–F3][S1 pp35,55,116,125]

Promises versus delivery:
- Dhule second 100 TPD plant: operating from November 2024; FY26 reported 82% throughput utilization. Real execution, with disclosed cost/time overruns and slower rCB qualification.
- Dhar target November–December 2025: actual commercial commencement May 2026 after consent. Delayed, not abandoned.
- Samsara October 2025 fire: company initially said mainly inventory, no serious plant/building damage, insured assets and no casualties; FY26 records ₹5.8194 crore loss including ₹0.1575 crore PPE. Restart May 2026, insurer receipt unverified.
- Syngas bottling: management pivoted toward sodium silicate after approval constraints. August 2026 target January 2027 remains prospective.
- J&K expansion: Green Valley exited rather than continued spending into geopolitical/subsidy uncertainty; abandonment can be prudent even though it reduces the original runway.
- One new plant annually: broad ambition only, not a completed/funded commitment. [S1][S8][S16][S19][S20][S22]

IPO fresh proceeds ₹44.925 crore were reported fully utilized by March 2025, including ₹17.8313 crore Maharashtra plant, ₹16.539 crore working capital, ₹6.7338 crore general purposes and ₹3.8209 crore expenses. They cannot be added again as current cash. Migration shareholder approval 12 October 2026 is not itself an exchange effectiveness notice. [S21][S10]

Integrating capital-advance movements gives FCFproxy−₹89.4859 crore, before financing interest and other investing effects. In FY26 alone, ₹52.667 crore gross PPE line less ₹21.3332 crore capital-advance release equals ₹31.3338 crore capital deployment; the release is not an extra profit or repeated source of cash. Expansion explains weak FCF, not automatically weak CFO. Historical cash bridges reconcile cash totals within source rounding, while individual cash classification/elimination still needs verification. [S1 pp102–103][S2 pp105–106][S3 pp133–135]

Material bridges:
- FY23 IPO versus later statutory: revenue ₹78.5241 versus ₹77.9472 crore, PAT ₹10.8478 versus ₹12.3506 crore, CFO ₹15.5311 versus ₹9.8595 crore. Reclassifying advances explains much but not a complete itemized bridge. Later comparable is used; old values remain visible.
- FY26 group cash-flow interest deducted/received ₹1.1739 crore versus group P&L interest ₹0.0132 crore: possible capitalized/intercompany elimination or classification, not automatically false cash. An auditor-backed ledger bridge is required.
- Fire inventory note differences ₹2.6328 crore raw plus ₹2.6519 crore finished exactly equal ₹5.2847 crore inventory write-off. This reconciles pre/post-fire inventory; it is not a second loss or an unexplained gap.
- Ordinary parent/group differences are expected: parent CFO ₹29.7348 crore is not substituted for group CFO ₹15.9696 crore. Subsidiary loans/investments are eliminated, not valued a second time.
- Consolidated cash-flow advances/GST/subsidy/tax reclassifications remain only partially mapped. Clean audit opinions and total cash reconciliation do not eliminate this material evidence gap. [S15][S3][S1]

IC reconciles operating and financing approaches to ₹0.0001 crore rounding, includes CWIP/goodwill/capital advances, and excludes cash, tax claims and financial investments consistently. Normalized ROIC6.35%, ROCE8.47%, ROE3.88%, interest cover 7.84× and netdebt/operating EBITDA 2.73× describe March economics, not current borrowing capacity. CARED/INC withdrawal and the later auditor’s no-default statement coexist; no current default is inferred. [S1][S4][S5]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹141 and 24.99 million shares, market value is ₹352.359 crore. Dividing by FY26 attributable PAT ₹3.4317 crore gives 102.68×; fire-adjusted P/E is not automatically sustainable. Using March debt/cash, operating EV is ₹415.5368 crore and EV/operating EBITDA is 17.97×. These are stale-balance illustrative multiples, not a live October enterprise value. AS lease obligations are not independently verified; operating rents remain in the modeled margin. [S1][M1][M2]

The principal valuation is a bottom-up operating model with six fiscal forecast labels but only five calendar years of post-entry cash flows. A separate March-to-October entry bridge is conditional, never historical fact. All annual sources/uses, working-capital changes, interest, tax, debt repayments and required cash are embedded in the canonical model. Base margins rise 18→21%, not management’s upper 25% aspiration; bear 11→13%, bull 21→24%. Exit EV/EBITDA 6×/9×/12× are analyst ranges, not observed comparable prices. [S16][model]

Every non-rescue path breaches the 1.5%-of-sales operating cash floor in the conditional FY27 pre-entry bridge. Ordinary IRRs and ordinary entry prices remain null because current funding is unverified; conditional non-rescue returns and entries are also null after the breach. Negative modeled cash is not silently converted into new debt. Separate rescue issues use ₹70.50/share, a 50% discount to the observed quote, plus 3% issuance fees; original shareholders are diluted. First rescue is hypothetical at entry and later issues occur at stated period ends. Base 9.02% is below 15%, bear −27.40% and bull 26.81% illustrate asymmetric execution outcomes, not scenario probabilities or ordinary forecasts.

Terminal equity subtracts all remaining bank/related debt and the residual gratuity claim and retains required operating cash; only cash above that floor contributes, with a signed shortfall in financing-agnostic diagnostics. No extra operating property, goodwill, prepaid project cash, IPO proceeds, subsidiary investment or insurance value is added. Legacy net current tax ₹3.3013 crore and accrued interest ₹0.0138 crore are settled once pre-entry, not deducted again at exit. Disputed ₹4.7748 crore tax is a separate stress, not paid and capitalized twice.

DCF uses 14/16/18% WACC,3/4/5% terminal growth and 10/14/18% terminal ROIC. Terminal reinvestment is next NOPAT× g/ROIC plus growth in operating cash; cash-floor reinvestment is also subtracted in the forecast. The equity bridge uses signed conditional entry cash less floor and entry debt, not the March balances. Values are labeled financing-agnostic, never an approved entry. Terminal-value share is disclosed for every cell and generally dominates, making point estimates fragile.

The reverse algebra requires a ₹283.60 terminal price to meet 15% with no dividends. Holding base debt/cash and 21% margin/9× multiple fixed implies roughly ₹357.09 crore terminal revenue, versus the bottom-up base about ₹288.81 crore. Alternatively it requires about 11.13× exit EBITDA. This is expectation algebra, not a newly solved funded path. The two-way margin/multiple grid reruns cash funding; hurdle sensitivity 12/15/18% is shown only for explicitly rescued cases. Additional capex, +5 percentage-point ONWC, loan calls, lost tax appeals, optional insurance recovery, rescue pricing/fees and execution costs are all separate linked sensitivities. No ordinary entry range is publishable until funding and reliability are resolved.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The critical thesis variable is the cash contribution of commissioned Dhar and maturing rCB output after incremental working capital and replacement investment, not the number of plants. The strongest counterargument to optimism is that FY26 throughput rose almost 50% but core group EBIT weakened, while debt increased and cash remained negligible. This may partly reflect commissioning and abnormal fire/tax charges, but those explanations do not provide cash to meet current obligations. [S1][S18]

Linked stress: crude-linked product prices weaken → new-plant utilization/rCB qualification disappoint → EBITDA margin compresses → customers and subsidy collections slow → inventories/GST claims absorb capital → banks or related lenders demand repayment → cheap equity issuance transfers upside away from existing owners. A single-offtaker silicate model reduces distribution effort but concentrates counterparty exposure. Imported feedstock/geopolitical logistics and environmental operating restrictions can worsen several variables together. [S1][S16][S22]

The explicit bear rescue needs roughly ₹43.29 crore gross new equity and 6.14 million shares; the resulting five-year return is about −27.40% annually. That is a modeled permanent-loss path, not merely a temporary quotation drawdown. Without that rescue the cash floor is breached, so a numerical ordinary bear return would be misleading. A cash-credit plus related-loan call, or lost tax appeal, worsens funding further. No insurance proceeds or subsidized receivable is assumed immediately realizable.

Impairment risk: High. Evidence of stable attributable Dhar/rCB cash returns, dated lender confirmation, successful insurance realization and full account bridges would reduce uncertainty. A one-quarter miss alone is not a thesis break; repeated inability to fund essential operations or evidence of serious minority harm would be. The market can already see the expansion/fire story. No informational edge or precise distress probability is claimed.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold price increase in five years needs 37.97% annualized price growth; tenfold needs 58.49%, or 25.89% overten years. These are arithmetic requirements, not forecasts. Earnings-based decompositions are fragile while reported PAT is fire/tax distorted; an EV-to-common-equity bridge is more informative. Enterprise growth does not equal per-share growth when new equity or related financing claims are required.

The current base uses three operating pyrolysis lines and a proposed silicate line, not an unlimited plant rollout. Even the bull explicitly models and funds a fourth line, stronger mix and larger equipment revenue; its rescued return does not establish 5× or 10×. A long-run multibagger thesis would require many repeated high-return plants, reliable customer qualification, environmental permissions, recoverable working capital and limited equity dilution, plus a non-heroic terminal multiple. Those plant/cohort returns and funding conditions are not verified. Classification: Speculative / unsupported. No numerical success probability, target price or portfolio allocation follows.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. Research priority is cash/funding verification and plant-attributable economics, not immediate purchase eligibility or an instruction to sell an existing holding. BQS/GQS/IAS are all NS; none may be ranked using the mathematical bounds or known-weight sums. The company does not meet the evidence-backed compounder designation. GOV 4 is not the ≤3 governance override, and historical CARE D/INC with later contradictory no-default evidence is not converted into a proven current G3 failure.

The price matters: ₹141 requires materially stronger performance/funding than the ordinary evidence can support, and even the separate base rescue is below the 15% hurdle. But a lower quote cannot cure missing cash reliability, unverified bank availability or absent CAP evidence. To reconsider: obtain current consolidated funds/limits/maturities, reconcile the material historical and intercompany cash bridges, quantify legacy MSME obligations, verify actual Dhar/silicate deployment and attributable returns, and confirm effective trading restrictions/depth for the actual position.

Existing holders face a different implementation problem from new buyers. Tax basis, portfolio concentration and personal objectives were not supplied; no trade, allocation or exit count is invented. Reported values are historical or explicitly conditional, not personalized investment advice. Both upside and downside remain contingent on evidence that is not yet established.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Material statements use primary issuer/exchange/rating sources and an evidence ledger distinguishing verified disclosures (V), calculations (C), management statements (M) and analyst assumptions (A). Audit language, rating limitations and company responses are preserved. Downloaded original-source digests support independent authentication; financial-only archives do not contain issuer PDFs, raw HTML, extracted/OCR text, page images or personal identifiers. Offline reproduction checks model consistency, not external truth or subsequent events.

Open questions are specific: current bank balances/undrawn facilities and demand-loan support; documentary bridge from FY23 restated to later statutory numbers; consolidated interest/cash reclassification; tax/MSME settlement status; project supplier payments versus capital-advance transfers; disclosed plant/cohort economics; insurance settlement; silicate offtake pricing/security; lease obligations; customer/supplier concentration and ownership/encumbrance updates after June. Missing answers remain ND/NS, never invented zero.

Valuation assumes 25% normalized operating tax, no automatic tax-loss monetization, cash floor 1.5% of TTM sales, disclosed March debt split, conditional bank/related rollover, explicit amortization and no ordinary new financing. Forecasts are not management commitments. DCF terminal reinvestment and operating cash are retained; no subsidiary, land, goodwill, IPO, prepaid capex or past-tax double counting is allowed. Fees/discounted dilution are explicit only in rescue cases; investor execution-cost sensitivity does not guarantee tradability.

Source-specific cautions: the RHP’s unquantified interest qualifications limit early earnings; CARE’s noncooperation methodology limits the fair-rating inference; shareholder migration approval is not effective listing migration; Google Drive results/transcript are authenticated as issuer-linked documents, not independently corroborated transactions; peer historical sources establish business mechanisms, not a live multiple screen.
